chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from al-Husayn ibn Khalid who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about congratulating someone on the birth of a child, asking when it should be done. He said: 'When al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was born, Jibril (peace be upon him) descended upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) with congratulations on the seventh day, and commanded him to name him, give him a kunya, shave his head, perform the 'aqiqah for him, and pierce his ear. And similarly, when al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was born, he came to him on the seventh day and commanded him to do the same.' He said: 'They both had two tufts of hair on the left horn (side of the head), and the piercing was in the right ear on the lobe, and in the left ear at the top, and the earring was in the right and the stud in the left.'
ai.seo_question: When should congratulation and birth rituals like 'aqiqah and ear piercing be performed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the Sunnah of the Prophet (peace be upon him) regarding the seventh-day rituals for al-Hasan and al-Husayn, emphasizing the divine instruction via Jibreel for naming, shaving, 'aqiqah, and ear piercing. It further provides specific biographical details about their physical appearance, particularly the 'dhawabat' (tufts of hair) and the distinct locations for ear piercing and jewelry, which serve as markers of their noble lineage and status in Shia tradition.
